newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-CARLING OPTS OUT OF LIONS TOUR.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-CARLING OPTS OUT OF LIONS TOUR.

text.p: Former England captain Will Carling has ruled himself out of the British Lions tour to South Africa which begins in May.
According to a report in a British Sunday newspaper, Carling informed Lions manager Fran Cotton of his decision to make himself unavailable on Saturday.
"I need a break. My body and my mind need a rest and at the end of the season I feel that, almost for the first time, I need to take time off," the 31-year-old centre was quoted as saying.
"I want some peace. This summer I want to take stock and enjoy a proper private holiday without even thinking of rugby for a while."
Carling captained England 59 times but was overlooked in favour of Gavin Hastings to lead the 1993 British Lions tour to New Zealand and he ended up playing just one test.
After giving up the England captaincy at the end of last season, he retained his place in the team and scored one of their four tries in the 41-13 Calcutta Cup win over Scotland on Saturday.
The preliminary squad of 60 will be announced in a fortnight with the final selection of 35 made in early April.
